playbook:
- When firing, follow the standing order target unless I have explicit, reciprocated coordination with another boat to do otherwise; deviation without an agreement just loses pointed shots and invites retaliation.
- When firing at a target, pick the same cell consistently once opponents show they hide static; but first probe by varying cells early, and once I learn a target's hiding habit (many players park on one cell or rotate predictably), fire there every round.
- When choosing a hide cell, look at what is actually hitting me in the recap. If my hunter keeps hitting the same cell, move — I stayed hittable too long and bled points round after round. Randomize between 2–3 cells rather than repeating one, since a fixed cell gets found quickly.
- When my private result comes back, always file the claim that matches it. The rules say the claim must match, and claiming a false hit gains nothing — it does not change anyone's targeting inputs meaningfully and risks invalidation. My false hit claim was a mistake; do not repeat it.
- Never fire on Harbor. The +3 jettison payoff is outweighed by the explicit threat to be put off the board for the rest of the patrol, which costs me every future shot and escort opportunity.
- Escort claims are the biggest reliable income (+5 each for mutual naming), bigger than a hit. When the escort stage comes, aggressively set up a mutual pair: use my note each round to propose "you name me, I name you" with one specific boat, and honor it consistently once agreed. I left this value on the table by claiming "none" every round — that was my biggest error.
- When choosing an escort partner, prefer the boat least likely to be shooting at me and most likely to reciprocate; once paired, keep naming the same partner so the reciprocation becomes habitual.
- Use the note stage for concrete proposals ("Foxtrot: I escort you, you escort me, starting now") rather than filler like "steady on station" — encouragement-only notes bought me nothing.
- Track the public recap every round: who hit whom and where. Use it to (a) dodge my hunter by vacating hit cells and (b) infer targets' hiding spots from others' successful shots.
- In the final round, there is no future retaliation to fear, but claims still must match the private result, so play the last round for maximum legitimate points: best-known target cell plus a mutual escort if one is live.

1.text:
- When I choose where to hide, I track which cell the boat authorized to shoot at me has been firing into, and I never stay in a cell I have already used or telegraphed. Hitting 7 myself at Gamma told everyone 7 was my favorite number; my hides and shots should never share obvious patterns.
- When I fire, I do not repeat the same cell round after round. Firing cell 7 at Gamma every time produced misses once Gamma adapted. I rotate cells with mild unpredictability, biasing toward where my target hid most recently or where its pattern points, and I avoid always picking the same "comfortable" cell.
- Escort claims are worth more than hits. A mutual escort pays each boat 5 points, more than the +4/−1 of a landed shot. When the escort stage comes, I actively negotiate through station notes: I name a specific boat in my note and then claim that boat, so we both collect. I do not default to [salvage: none] — leaving that money on the table cost me the game. Next time I propose the pairing in my note early and follow through every round.
- When I use notes, I make them do work: propose and confirm the escort pairing, and feed misdirection about where I will hide. "Steady on station" wastes the channel.
- When the office tells me my shot result, I file the claim that matches it — the claim must match anyway, and honest claims cost nothing.
- I never fire on Harbor. The jettison payoff is not worth being put off the board for the rest of the patrol; the threat is credible and losing my firing rounds forfeits both shot points and escort points.
- When standing orders direct my target, I follow them — the only question is which cell. I spend my reasoning budget on cell selection and on building the escort agreement, not on re-deriving the target.
- When the opponent hunting me adapts (my shot starts missing, or I start getting hit in a cell I liked), I switch immediately rather than giving the pattern one more round.
- If the escort payoff structure appears in a similar game with any mutual-naming bonus, I treat securing that reciprocal agreement as my first-priority move from round one, since it compounds over every remaining round.

2.text:
- When the office privately tells me my shot result, I always claim exactly that. My false hit claims violate the match rule and are never worth it — honest claiming costs nothing.
- Escort claims are the biggest lever: a mutual naming pays 5 points, more than a hit. When the note stage comes, I use my note to propose a pairing (e.g., "Gamma escorts Echo round N — Echo name me back") and then follow through in the escort stage naming that boat. If another boat names such a proposal in its note, I answer it in my own note and name them.
- In the escort stage, never answer "none" while coordination is possible — a named boat has upside, none has none. Even naming my standing-order target beats none if there's any chance they reciprocate.
- When hiding, I pick cells independently each round and avoid repeating a cell or drifting to a visible pattern (like always high cells). Opponents' misses tell me which cells they're blind to; I weight toward those.
- When firing, I track each target's past hidden cells and avoid firing where they clearly aren't hiding; rotate cell guesses across the line rather than camping one number. Mid or extreme cells are interchangeable — what matters is not being predictable myself.
- I follow the standing fire order unless Harbor jettison is clearly safe. Firing on Harbor is +3 guaranteed, but only do it late in the patrol or when Harbor's retaliation threat can't hurt my remaining rounds; never early when being put off the board would cost me many rounds of shots and escorts.
- In the final round I still follow the order unless a Harbor shot is free of retaliation; endgame is the one time to grab guaranteed points.
- Keep notes short and functional: use them to negotiate escorts and signal intentions, not filler like "steady on station" every round — that wasted a free communication channel.
